question: A farmer needs to transport 1000 units of fresh agricultural products from the farm to a nearby market. The farmer has three transportation options: horses, bicycles, and hand carts. Due to the physical exertion required for bicycles and hand carts, the farmer only wants to choose one of these two transportation methods. Horses produce 80 units of pollution per trip, bicycles produce 0 units of pollution, and hand carts produce 0 units of pollution. The total pollution generated by all trips must not exceed 1000 units. The farmer needs to use horses for at least 8 trips. Horses, bicycles, and hand carts can each carry 55 units, 30 units, and 40 units of products per trip, respectively. The farmer needs to ensure that the total quantity of transported products is at least 1000 units.

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# =====================================================================
# DECISION VARIABLES
#   trips[m]  m in MODES = {horses, bicycles, handcarts}
#             NonNegativeIntegers, number of trips made by each mode.
#   use_bike  Binary, =1 if bicycles are the chosen non-horse mode.
#   use_cart  Binary, =1 if hand carts are the chosen non-horse mode.
#
# OBJECTIVE (minimize): total pollution = 80*trips[horses]
#                       (bicycles and hand carts emit 0 pollution).
#
# CONSTRAINTS
#   (1) Demand: 55*trips[horses] + 30*trips[bicycles] + 40*trips[handcarts]
#               >= 1000                       [source: "at least 1000 units"]
#   (2) Pollution cap: 80*trips[horses] <= 1000
#               [source: "total pollution ... must not exceed 1000 units"]
#   (3) Horse minimum: trips[horses] >= 8
#               [source: "use horses for at least 8 trips"]
#   (4) Exclusive choice: use_bike + use_cart <= 1
#               [source: "only wants to choose one of these two methods"]
#   (5) Link bicycles: trips[bicycles] <= M * use_bike
#   (6) Link hand carts: trips[handcarts] <= M * use_cart
# =====================================================================

DATA = {
    "demand_units":          1000,   # must transport >= 1000 units
    "poll_cap":              1000,   # pollution total <= 1000
    "horse_min_trips":          8,   # at least 8 horse trips
    "cap_horses":              55,   # capacity per trip
    "cap_bicycles":            30,
    "cap_handcarts":           40,
    "poll_horses":             80,   # pollution per horse trip
    "poll_bicycles":            0,
    "poll_handcarts":           0,
    "bikes_or_cart_at_most":    1,   # choose at most one of the two
    "big_m_trips":             40,   # upper bound on trips of a chosen mode
}

MODES = ["horses", "bicycles", "handcarts"]


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ----- sets -------------------------------------------------------
    m.MODES = pyo.Set(initialize=MODES)

    # ----- decision variables ----------------------------------------
    m.trips = pyo.Var(m.MODES, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    m.use_bike = pyo.Var(within=pyo.Binary)
    m.use_cart = pyo.Var(within=pyo.Binary)

    # ----- objective: minimize total pollution ------------------------
    def obj_rule(m):
        return d["poll_horses"] * m.trips["horses"] \
             + d["poll_bicycles"] * m.trips["bicycles"] \
             + d["poll_handcarts"] * m.trips["handcarts"]
    m.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ----- (1) demand satisfaction ------------------------------------
    def demand_rule(m):
        return (d["cap_horses"] * m.trips["horses"]
                + d["cap_bicycles"] * m.trips["bicycles"]
                + d["cap_handcarts"] * m.trips["handcarts"]) >= d["demand_units"]
    m.demand = pyo.Constraint(rule=demand_rule)

    # ----- (2) pollution cap ------------------------------------------
    def pollution_rule(m):
        return d["poll_horses"] * m.trips["horses"] <= d["poll_cap"]
    m.pollution = pyo.Constraint(rule=pollution_rule)

    # ----- (3) minimum horse trips ------------------------------------
    def horse_min_rule(m):
        return m.trips["horses"] >= d["horse_min_trips"]
    m.horse_min = pyo.Constraint(rule=horse_min_rule)

    # ----- (4) exclusive choice between bicycles and hand carts -------
    def exclusive_rule(m):
        return m.use_bike + m.use_cart <= d["bikes_or_cart_at_most"]
    m.exclusive = pyo.Constraint(rule=exclusive_rule)

    # ----- (5) link bicycles trips to use_bike ------------------------
    def link_bike_rule(m):
        return m.trips["bicycles"] <= d["big_m_trips"] * m.use_bike
    m.link_bike = pyo.Constraint(rule=link_bike_rule)

    # ----- (6) link hand cart trips to use_cart -----------------------
    def link_cart_rule(m):
        return m.trips["handcarts"] <= d["big_m_trips"] * m.use_cart
    m.link_cart = pyo.Constraint(rule=link_cart_rule)

    return m

    "i_horse": 0,
    "i_bike": 1,
    "i_cart": 2,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Sets
    model.M = pyo.Set(initialize=d["modes"])

    # Variables: number of trips per mode
    model.x = pyo.Var(
        model.M,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=lambda m, i: (d["horse_min_trips"], None) if i == d["i_horse"] else (0, None),
    )

    # Binary choice variables for the mutually exclusive pair (bike vs cart)
    model.y = pyo.Var([d["i_bike"], d["i_cart"]], within=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: minimize total pollution (only horses pollute here)
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["pollution_per_trip"][i] * m.x[i] for i in m.M)
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Demand: total products transported >= 1000
    def demand_rule(m):
        return sum(d["cap_per_trip"][i] * m.x[i] for i in m.M) >= d["total_products_min"]
    model.demand = pyo.Constraint(rule=demand_rule)

    # Pollution cap: total pollution <= 1000
    def pollution_rule(m):
        return sum(d["pollution_per_trip"][i] * m.x[i] for i in m.M) <= d["pollution_max"]
    model.pollution = pyo.Constraint(rule=pollution_rule)

    # Horse minimum: at least 8 horse trips (also enforced via bound, kept explicit here)
    def horse_min_rule(m):
        return m.x[d["i_horse"]] >= d["horse_min_trips"]
    model.horse_min = pyo.Constraint(rule=horse_min_rule)

    # Mutual exclusivity: only one of bicycles / hand carts may be used
    def excl_rule(m):
        return m.y[d["i_bike"]] + m.y[d["i_cart"]] <= 1
    model.exclusive = pyo.Constraint(rule=excl_rule)

    # Big-M linking: trips of a mode must be zero if that mode is not chosen
    def link_rule(m, i):
        return m.x[i] <= d["big_m"] * m.y[i]
    model.link = pyo.Constraint([d["i_bike"], d["i_cart"]], rule=link_rule)

    return model

    "capacity_per_trip": {"horses": 55, "bicycles": 30, "hand_carts": 40},
    "pollution_per_trip": {"horses": 80, "bicycles": 0, "hand_carts": 0},
    "min_horse_trips": 8,

    "big_M": 1000,  # upper bound on trips of any mode
    "exclusive_modes": ["bicycles", "hand_carts"],
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.MODES = pyo.Set(initialize=d["modes"])
    model.EXCLUSIVE = pyo.Set(initialize=d["exclusive_modes"])

    # Decision variables: number of trips per mode (integer, >= 0)
    model.trips = pyo.Var(
        model.MODES,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=(0, d["big_M"]),
    )

    # Binary selector for the mutually exclusive modes
    model.mode_choice = pyo.Var(model.EXCLUSIVE, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: minimise total pollution
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(
            d["pollution_per_trip"][mode] * m.trips[mode] for mode in m.MODES
        )

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Total pollution must not exceed the cap
    def pollution_cap_rule(m):
        return sum(
            d["pollution_per_trip"][mode] * m.trips[mode] for mode in m.MODES
        ) <= d["max_total_pollution"]

    model.pollution_cap = pyo.Constraint(rule=pollution_cap_rule)

    # Horses used for at least the minimum number of trips
    def min_horse_trips_rule(m):
        return m.trips["horses"] >= d["min_horse_trips"]

    model.min_horse_trips = pyo.Constraint(rule=min_horse_trips_rule)

    # Total transported product must meet the demand
    def product_demand_rule(m):
        return sum(
            d["capacity_per_trip"][mode] * m.trips[mode] for mode in m.MODES
        ) >= d["min_total_products"]

    model.product_demand = pyo.Constraint(rule=product_demand_rule)

    # At most one of the exclusive modes may be used
    def exclusive_choice_rule(m):
        return sum(m.mode_choice[mode] for mode in m.EXCLUSIVE) <= 1

    model.exclusive_choice = pyo.Constraint(rule=exclusive_choice_rule)

    # Link trip counts to the binary selectors via big-M
    def link_choice_rule(m, mode):
        return m.trips[mode] <= d["big_M"] * m.mode_choice[mode]

    model.link_choice = pyo.Constraint(model.EXCLUSIVE, rule=link_choice_rule)

    return model

DATA = {
    "DEMAND": 1000,             # units of products that must be transported
    "POLLUTION_LIMIT": 1000,    # max total pollution
    "HORSE_MIN_TRIPS": 8,       # at least this many horse trips
    "HORSE_POLLUTION": 80,      # pollution per horse trip
    "BICYCLE_POLLUTION": 0,     # pollution per bicycle trip
    "CART_POLLUTION": 0,        # pollution per hand-cart trip
    "HORSE_LOAD": 55,           # units carried per horse trip
    "BICYCLE_LOAD": 30,         # units carried per bicycle trip
    "CART_LOAD": 40,            # units carried per hand-cart trip
    "BIG_M": 1000,              # valid upper bound on trips of any single mode
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ----- Sets -------------------------------------------------------------
    # Mode 1 = horses, 2 = bicycles, 3 = hand carts
    m.THREE = pyo.Set(initialize=[1, 2, 3])
    # The two modes subject to the "choose only one" restriction
    m.PAIR = pyo.Set(initialize=[2, 3])

    # ----- Variables --------------------------------------------------------
    # Number of trips taken by each mode
    m.x = pyo.Var(m.THREE, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # Binary selector: 1 if the mode is used, 0 otherwise
    m.y = pyo.Var(m.PAIR, within=pyo.Binary)

    # ----- Objective: minimise total pollution ------------------------------
    def obj_rule(m):
        return (
            d["HORSE_POLLUTION"] * m.x[1]
            + d["BICYCLE_POLLUTION"] * m.x[2]
            + d["CART_POLLUTION"] * m.x[3]
        )

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ----- Constraints ------------------------------------------------------
    # Total transported products must be AT LEAST the demand  (>=)
    def demand_rule(m):
        return (
            d["HORSE_LOAD"] * m.x[1]
            + d["BICYCLE_LOAD"] * m.x[2]
            + d["CART_LOAD"] * m.x[3]
            >= d["DEMAND"]
        )

    m.demand = pyo.Constraint(rule=demand_rule)

    # Total pollution must NOT exceed the limit  (<=)
    def pollution_rule(m):
        return (
            d["HORSE_POLLUTION"] * m.x[1]
            + d["BICYCLE_POLLUTION"] * m.x[2]
            + d["CART_POLLUTION"] * m.x[3]
            <= d["POLLUTION_LIMIT"]
        )

    m.pollution = pyo.Constraint(rule=pollution_rule)

    # Horses must be used for AT LEAST the stated number of trips  (>=)
    def horse_min_rule(m):
        return m.x[1] >= d["HORSE_MIN_TRIPS"]

    m.horse_min = pyo.Constraint(rule=horse_min_rule)

    # Choose at most one of bicycles / hand carts -> exactly one if either used
    def choose_one_rule(m):
        return m.y[2] + m.y[3] == 1

    m.choose_one = pyo.Constraint(rule=choose_one_rule)

    # Big-M linking: a mode's trip count is 0 unless its selector is 1  (<=)
    def link_rule(m, i):
        return m.x[i] <= d["BIG_M"] * m.y[i]

    m.link = pyo.Constraint(m.PAIR, rule=link_rule)

    # Bicycles and hand carts produce no pollution, so they are never "used"
    # in a pollution-minimising sense unless forced; the selector enforces
    # the either/or structural requirement.
    return m

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Decision variables
#   x[m] : number of trips made by transportation mode m
#          m in {"horses", "bicycles", "handcarts"}, domain NonNegativeIntegers
#   y[b] : binary selector for the bicycle/handcart pair
#          b in {"bicycles", "handcarts"}, domain Binary
#          y[b] = 1 means mode b is used (trips may be > 0)
#
# Objective (in words)
#   Minimise total pollution produced by all trips.
#   Pollution per trip: horses 80, bicycles 0, handcarts 0.
#
# Constraints (numbered, with source sentence)
#   (1) Demand: total transported product >= 1000 units.
#       "The farmer needs to ensure that the total quantity of transported
#        products is at least 1000 units."
#   (2) Pollution cap: total pollution <= 1000 units.
#       "The total pollution generated by all trips must not exceed 1000 units."
#   (3) Horse minimum: trips by horses >= 8.
#       "The farmer needs to use horses for at least 8 trips."
#   (4) Exclusive choice: at most one of bicycles / handcarts is used.
#       "the farmer only wants to choose one of these two transportation methods."
#       Linearised with big-M: x[b] <= M * y[b] for each b, and
#       y[bicycles] + y[handcarts] <= 1.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DATA = {
    "modes": ["horses", "bicycles", "handcarts"],
    "capacity": {"horses": 55, "bicycles": 30, "handcarts": 40},
    "pollution": {"horses": 80, "bicycles": 0, "handcarts": 0},
    "demand": 1000,
    "pollution_cap": 1000,
    "horse_min_trips": 8,
    "exclusive_pair": ["bicycles", "handcarts"],
    "big_m_trips": 10000,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    modes = d["modes"]
    pair = d["exclusive_pair"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.M = pyo.Set(initialize=modes, ordered=True)
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=pair, ordered=True)

    # x[m]: trips per mode, non-negative integers
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.M, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # y[b]: binary selector for the exclusive bicycle/handcart pair
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.Binary)

    # (1) Demand: total transported product >= 1000
    def demand_rule(m):
        return sum(d["capacity"][i] * m.x[i] for i in m.M) >= d["demand"]
    model.demand = pyo.Constraint(rule=demand_rule)

    # (2) Pollution cap: total pollution <= 1000
    def pollution_rule(m):
        return sum(d["pollution"][i] * m.x[i] for i in m.M) <= d["pollution_cap"]
    model.pollution = pyo.Constraint(rule=pollution_rule)

    # (3) Horse minimum: trips by horses >= 8
    def horse_min_rule(m):
        return m.x["horses"] >= d["horse_min_trips"]
    model.horse_min = pyo.Constraint(rule=horse_min_rule)

    # (4a) Link trips to selector: x[b] <= M * y[b]
    def link_rule(m, b):
        return m.x[b] <= d["big_m_trips"] * m.y[b]
    model.link = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=link_rule)

    # (4b) At most one of the pair is used
    def exclusive_rule(m):
        return sum(m.y[b] for b in m.P) <= 1
    model.exclusive = pyo.Constraint(rule=exclusive_rule)

    # Objective: minimise total pollution
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["pollution"][i] * m.x[i] for i in m.M)
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return model
